### `build-code-unsafe`

- **Level**: WARNING.
- **Means**: --allow-build lists a project's files by running a real PEP 517
  build of its wheel, which executes the project's own build code (its build
  backend and any script the backend runs) with the user's rights, for up to
  --build-timeout seconds. Said before each build: for a build backend no file
  discoverer of Pitloom reads, or after the backend's own discoverer failed; in
  a fresh, isolated build environment, or in Pitloom's own with
  --no-build-isolation.
- **SBOM effect**: none: the SBOM states what the input holds.
- **Pitloom did**: Ran the build and read the file list from the wheel it wrote.
- **Tell the user**: Pitloom ran the project's own build code, as --allow-build
  asks; run it only on a project they trust. Do not pass --allow-build for them
  on a project they have not chosen to build; ask first, and with nobody to ask,
  report it only.
- **Printed after**: `Build: <text>` (--allow-build: the build and its temporary
  directories), on its WARNING lines; the prefix is not part of the line.
- **Lines**:

  ```text
  WARNING: DIR=<dir>: --allow-build runs a PEP 517 build for up to <duration> (--build-timeout), which executes the project's build code (build-backend <backend>, no discovery module for it) in an isolated build environment [build-code-unsafe]
  WARNING: DIR=<dir>: --allow-build runs a PEP 517 build for up to <duration> (--build-timeout), which executes the project's build code (build-backend <backend>, its static discovery failed) in an isolated build environment [build-code-unsafe]
  WARNING: DIR=<dir>: --allow-build runs a PEP 517 build for up to <duration> (--build-timeout), which executes the project's build code (build-backend <backend>, no discovery module for it) in Pitloom's own environment (no build isolation) [build-code-unsafe]
  WARNING: DIR=<dir>: --allow-build runs a PEP 517 build for up to <duration> (--build-timeout), which executes the project's build code (build-backend <backend>, its static discovery failed) in Pitloom's own environment (no build isolation) [build-code-unsafe]
  ```

### `build-failed`

- **Level**: WARNING.
- **Means**: The --allow-build build gave no wheel to read: no Python
  interpreter to run PyPA build with, the build exited with an error (its last
  line of output shown, a credential in it masked), it wrote no wheel or
  several, its wheel holds no file outside .dist-info, or the build could not
  start or its wheel could not be read (the reason shown). A build cut off by
  --build-timeout is build-timeout; PyPA build not installed is library-missing.
- **SBOM effect**: weaker: what the SBOM says is less sure.
- **Pitloom did**: Went on without the build: the file discovery line that
  follows says which fallback listed the files.
- **Tell the user**: the build failed and why, as the line says, and that the
  file list comes from the fallback the next line names. They fix the build
  (python -m build --wheel in the project shows its whole output) and run again,
  or drop --allow-build. Do not change the project or run its build for them;
  ask first, and with nobody to ask, report it only.
- **Printed after**: `Build: <text>` (--allow-build: the build and its temporary
  directories), on its WARNING lines; the prefix is not part of the line.
- **Lines**:

  ```text
  WARNING: DIR=<dir>: no Python interpreter to run PyPA build with; not built [build-failed]
  WARNING: DIR=<dir>: the build exited with code <exit-code>; last output: <output> [build-failed]
  WARNING: DIR=<dir>: the build wrote <number> wheels, not one [build-failed]
  WARNING: DIR=<dir>: the built wheel holds no file outside .dist-info; read as a failed discovery [build-failed]
  WARNING: DIR=<dir>: the build could not run or its wheel could not be read; <failure> [build-failed]
  ```

### `build-processes-unsafe`

- **Level**: WARNING, INFO.
- **Means**: The build ended and left processes it started still running in its
  process group (a backend's background helper): third-party code that would go
  on writing into the build's directory. POSIX only.
- **SBOM effect**: none: the SBOM states what the input holds.
- **Pitloom did**: Killed them before removing the build's directory (the INFO:
  line); on the WARNING: line, could not confirm they stopped. The build's
  result is read as usual.
- **Tell the user**: only of the WARNING: line: processes the build started may
  still be running, in the process group the line names; they check and stop
  them. The INFO: line needs nothing. Do not stop processes for them; ask first,
  and with nobody to ask, report it only.
- **Printed after**: `Build: <text>` (--allow-build: the build and its temporary
  directories), on its WARNING and INFO lines; the prefix is not part of the
  line.
- **Lines**:

  ```text
  INFO: the build left processes running (process group <process-group>); killed [build-processes-unsafe]
  WARNING: the build left processes running (process group <process-group>); could not confirm they stopped [build-processes-unsafe]
  ```

### `build-timeout`

- **Level**: WARNING.
- **Means**: The --allow-build build ran longer than --build-timeout allows (a
  slow build, or one waiting for the network or for input). Its process tree was
  stopped; on the second line Pitloom could not confirm every process of it
  ended.
- **SBOM effect**: weaker: what the SBOM says is less sure.
- **Pitloom did**: Went on without the build: the file discovery line that
  follows says which fallback listed the files.
- **Tell the user**: the build was stopped at the time limit. They run again
  with a larger --build-timeout for a slow build, or check that the build does
  not wait for input; after the second line, processes of the build may still
  run, and they check for them. Do not raise the limit or stop processes for
  them; ask first, and with nobody to ask, report it only.
- **Printed after**: `Build: <text>` (--allow-build: the build and its temporary
  directories), on its WARNING lines; the prefix is not part of the line.
- **Lines**:

  ```text
  WARNING: DIR=<dir>: the build timed out after <duration> (--build-timeout); its process tree was stopped [build-timeout]
  WARNING: DIR=<dir>: the build timed out after <duration> (--build-timeout); could not confirm its process tree stopped [build-timeout]
  ```

### `hook-no-effect`

- **Level**: INFO.
- **Means**: The Hatchling build hook ran for a build it makes no SBOM for: its
  table [tool.hatch.build.hooks.pitloom] sets enabled = false, the build target
  is not the wheel (an sdist: PEP 770 places an SBOM in a wheel's
  .dist-info/sboms/ only), or the wheel is an editable one, which holds a .pth
  file, not the project's files the SBOM would list.
- **SBOM effect**: none: the SBOM states what the input holds.
- **Pitloom did**: Staged no SBOM for this build; the build goes on.
- **Nothing to do**: Nothing to fix: the build is one the hook leaves alone. For
  an SBOM in the wheel, the user builds a regular (not editable) wheel with the
  hook enabled; mention it only when they ask why the wheel or sdist holds no
  SBOM.
- **Printed after**: `Pitloom build hook: <text>` (the Hatchling build hook, its
  own warnings and notes), on its INFO lines; the prefix is not part of the
  line.
- **Lines**:

  ```text
  INFO: disabled; skipping SBOM generation [hook-no-effect]
  INFO: target <target> is not 'wheel'; skipping SBOM generation [hook-no-effect]
  INFO: build variant 'editable' skipped; its wheel does not hold the project's files [hook-no-effect]
  ```

### `interrupted`

- **Level**: ERROR, WARNING. As an ERROR (Ctrl-C), the command stops and writes
  nothing (exit 130).
- **Means**: Pitloom was asked to stop. The WARNING: lines: a termination signal
  (SIGTERM, SIGHUP, or SIGBREAK for Ctrl-Break) came while a build or the copy
  of a model file out of a wheel ran, or after it while its temporary
  directories were in use; the process then ends by that signal (exit status 143
  for SIGTERM). The ERROR: line: Ctrl-C (exit status 130).
- **SBOM effect**: not-written: no SBOM is written for the input.
- **Pitloom did**: Stopped the run (a build or a model file copy, when one was
  running), removed its temporary directories and wrote no SBOM.
- **Tell the user**: the run was stopped before it wrote an SBOM. They run it
  again when ready. Do not run it again for them; ask first, and with nobody to
  ask, report it only.
- **Printed after**: `Build: <text>` (--allow-build: the build and its temporary
  directories), on its WARNING lines; the prefix is not part of the line.
- **Printed after**: `AI model scan: <text>` (the AI model scan of a wheel, its
  temporary copy), on its WARNING lines; the prefix is not part of the line.
- **Lines**:

  ```text
  WARNING: received <signal> during <activity>; exiting after cleanup [interrupted]
  WARNING: received <signal> after <activity>; exiting after cleanup [interrupted]
  ERROR: interrupted [interrupted]
  ```

### `temp-dir-unwritable`

- **Level**: WARNING.
- **Means**: A temporary directory Pitloom made (a download, a Git checkout, a
  build, a copy of a model file, the build hook's staged SBOM) could not be
  fully removed: a file in it still open (Windows), or no permission to remove
  it. The line names the directory by its name, not its path: it is in the
  system temp directory. The prefix says which step made it.
- **SBOM effect**: none: the SBOM states what the input holds.
- **Pitloom did**: Left what remained; the run goes on and its output is
  unchanged.
- **Tell the user**: a temporary directory was left behind, as the line names
  it; they delete it from the system temp directory once nothing uses it. Do not
  delete files for them; ask first, and with nobody to ask, report it only.
- **Printed after**: `Git source: <text>` (a Git URL fetch), on its WARNING
  lines; the prefix is not part of the line.
- **Printed after**: `Build: <text>` (--allow-build: the build and its temporary
  directories), on its WARNING lines; the prefix is not part of the line.
- **Printed after**: `Hugging Face source: <text>` (a Hugging Face model fetch,
  its temporary directory), on its WARNING lines; the prefix is not part of the
  line.
- **Printed after**: `PyPI source: <text>` (a PyPI URL download, its temporary
  directory), on its WARNING lines; the prefix is not part of the line.
- **Printed after**: `AI model scan: <text>` (the AI model scan of a wheel, its
  temporary copy), on its WARNING lines; the prefix is not part of the line.
- **Printed after**: `Pitloom build hook: <text>` (the Hatchling build hook, its
  own warnings and notes), on its WARNING lines; the prefix is not part of the
  line.
- **Lines**:

  ```text
  WARNING: DIR=<dir>: could not be fully removed; left in the system temp directory [temp-dir-unwritable]
  ```

## Summaries

A summary is an `INFO:` line that reports what a run did under its own rule (a
count, the key it wrote), with no condition to name: it carries no code, and
there is nothing to do.

- The build hook made the wheel's SBOM and staged it under the file name shown,
  with the number of [tool.pitloom.fragment] files merged into it; Hatchling
  places it in the wheel's .dist-info/sboms/ (PEP 770).

  ```text
  INFO: Pitloom build hook: staged SBOM '<path>' (<number> fragment(s)); Hatchling will inject it into .dist-info/sboms/ in the wheel
  ```
